title: Chichinga
author: Fran Osseo-Asare
desc: Twelve ounces of beef cut into eighteen to twenty-one strips, shaken six at a time in half a cup of tankora, three to a skewer.
longDesc: Chichinga is the Ghanaian kebab, known as kyinkyinga and as tsire suya in Nigeria, and this is the step-by-step version. Twelve ounces of tender beef is cut into eighteen to twenty-one strips a quarter to three-eighths of an inch thick, marinated about half an hour in tomato paste, pepper, ginger, garlic, grated onion, salt, white pepper and oil, then shaken six pieces at a time in a bag with half a cup of tankora powder. Three pieces per skewer, brushed with peanut oil, broiled five minutes, turned, five minutes more. Serves three.
ingredients: 12 oz tender beef — top round or London broil
Bamboo skewers — not the long ones
Ground dried red pepper, about 1/3-1/2 tsp
About 1/4 to 1/3 onion, grated — to get 1 1/2 to 2 tbsp
About 1 tsp salt or seasoned salt
About 1/2 tsp white or black pepper
steps: Soak the bamboo skewers at least 1 hour.
Cut the beef into 18 to 21 strips, a quarter to three-eighths of an inch thick.
Mix the marinade and coat the strips.
Refrigerate about half an hour or longer.
Shake 6 pieces at a time in half a cup of tankora in a bag.
Broil 5 minutes, turn, and broil another 5 minutes.
chefTips: Shake six pieces at a time in the bag rather than all at once. The tankora coats evenly that way and you do not end up with bare patches and clumps.
Soak the skewers at least an hour or they char through under a broiler.
Not the long skewers — her own note. Three pieces of meat on a short skewer is the street-food proportion.
A quarter to three-eighths of an inch thick. Thicker and the ten minutes will not cook it; thinner and it dries out.
Half an hour in the marinade or longer. This is not an overnight marinade — the tankora does the heavy flavour work.
Brush with peanut oil before broiling. It helps the coating stick and crisp rather than scorch.
A chicken version is published alongside: twelve ounces of boneless breast or thigh, same procedure, same eighteen to twenty-one strips.
commonMistakes: Coating all the meat at once.
sources: Adapted from 'Recipe #40: Step-by-step Chichinga (Kyinkyinga/Tsire Suya)', betumiblog.blogspot.com, Friday 5 February 2010. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'Posted by Fran'. The post URL redirect-loops, so it was read via the month archive page. YIELD as printed: Version I (beef) 'serves 3 people'; Version II (chicken) 'serves 3'.

INTRO, verbatim and confirmed on both passes: 'what is known in Ghana as chichinga... This popular street food, appetizer, and party snack is common throughout West Africa. In Nigeria this version of kebab is called tsire suya.'

Beef version, ingredients exactly as printed and TWO-PASS: 12 ounces tender beef (top round/London broil); bamboo skewers (NOT the long ones); 1/2 cup tankora powder. Marinade: 1-2 teaspoons tomato paste; ground dried red pepper to taste (about 1/3-1/2 teaspoon); ~1/2 teaspoon fresh grated ginger; ~1/2 teaspoon garlic; about 1/4 to 1/3 onion, grated (to get 1 1/2 - 2 tablespoons); ~1 teaspoon salt or seasoned salt; ~1/2 teaspoon white or black pepper; 2 teaspoons vegetable oil.
CHICKEN VERSION as printed: 12 ounces boneless chicken (breast and/or thigh), same procedure, 18-21 strips.

Method, SINGLE-PASS detail: soak skewers at least 1 hour; cut into 18-21 strips (1/4-3/8 inch thick); refrigerate marinated about half an hour or longer; shake 6 pieces at a time in 1/2 cup tankora in a bag; thread 3 pieces per skewer; brush with peanut oil; broil 5 minutes, turn, broil 'another 5 minutes'.
NO SENSORY DONENESS CUE is printed — only the 5-plus-5-minute broiling. That absence is recorded rather than filled in.

THREE DOCUMENTED CHICHINGA, from three named cooks, agreeing on almost nothing except the skewer. THIS ONE: beef, a tomato-paste marinade, and a tankora coating of ground kulikuli peanuts and toasted corn flour. ERIC ADJEPONG (GHA062): sirloin, a two-blend system including 10 Maggi cubes and peanut butter powder, grilled. ZOE ADJONYOH (GHA063): GOAT, with a wet rub of 125 g ground roasted peanuts, no corn flour and no Maggi. The meat, the spice system and the cooking method all differ. NOT RECONCILED.
The tankora powder this recipe depends on is published at GHA064, from the same author's adjacent post.
storage: Best eaten at once. 2 days refrigerated cooked.
healthBenefits: Lean beef is high in protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12.
The peanut-based tankora adds niacin, vitamin E and monounsaturated fat.
culturalNote: Chichinga is sold from charcoal grills on Accra street corners after dark, three pieces to a stick, with extra tankora dusted on at the last moment. That the same kebab is tsire suya across the border in Nigeria, with a nearly identical peanut-and-spice coating, is one of the clearest pieces of shared food culture in West Africa.
